report:
## Conclusion

Yes — the weight of evidence supports that widespread mask wearing reduces community-level SARS-CoV-2 transmission, though the size of the effect and confidence vary by study design.

**Strongest evidence:** The largest real-world test is a cluster-randomized trial in rural Bangladesh (~340,000 people), which found that promoting mask use raised community mask-wearing and reduced symptomatic seroprevalence overall (~9%), with a clearer effect for surgical masks (~11%) and especially among adults over 50–60 (23–35% reduction) (https://www.eurekalert.org/news-releases/936726). This is considered the best causal evidence to date because it randomized an intervention rather than merely observing mask use.

**Observational/ecological evidence:** A PNAS analysis using detailed data on self-reported mask-wearing (rather than mandates alone) found that population-level mask use was associated with meaningfully lower transmission — the average U.S. mask-wearing level corresponded to roughly a 19% reduction in the virus's effective reproduction number (https://www.pnas.org/doi/10.1073/pnas.2119266119). A broader narrative review in PNAS similarly concluded masks reduce transmission risk, citing mechanistic (filtration), epidemiological, and ecological data (https://www.pnas.org/doi/10.1073/pnas.2014564118).

**Caveat — the Cochrane review:** A widely publicized 2023 Cochrane review of RCTs found the evidence "uncertain," not that masks don't work; the trials it pooled were heterogeneous, mostly measured mandates/promotion rather than actual mask-wearing, and had compliance and design limitations. Cochrane's editor-in-chief later clarified this was misrepresented in media as "masks don't work" (https://www.cochrane.org/about-us/news/statement-physical-interventions-interrupt-or-reduce-spread-respiratory-viruses-review).

**Bottom line:** High-quality trial and observational data converge on a modest-to-moderate protective effect at the population level, strongest for well-fitted surgical/respirator-grade masks and high compliance, while trial-level uncertainty reflects methodological challenges rather than proof of no effect.
